Cause was readBody leaving its for-await loop, which destroys the request and the socket after the 413 had been advertised keep-alive. divergence: HEAD answers a GET route's headers without its body (r004, r187, r188 200 as the oracle); a route with no GET has no HEAD (405). Not matched, deliberately: POST with a raw body is accepted on /tika, /rmeta, /meta and /detect where the oracle answers 405 (r059, r108, r130, r148), and /unpack takes it where the oracle answers 415 (r174); the 405 Allow header names that route's own methods, where the oracle's is one list for every route.
note: tikajs-68os.7.8: more permissive than Tika, no Tika client is affected; documented in docs/migration.md. Not run against a live Tika.

upstream: Path matching: trailing slash, dot segments, case
divergence: A trailing slash is ignored on every route (r007, r083, r103 200 as the oracle). A path that starts with // is a 400 (r192, as the oracle; new URL had taken it for a host and answered 404). A path with a . or .. segment (raw or %2e) is a 404 and is not folded into another route (oracle 404; rip had folded /tika/../version to /version). Uppercase paths are 404 in both (r193).
note: tikajs-68os.7.8: parseTarget in packages/server/src/index.ts. Not run against a live Tika.

divergence: rip survived all probes. Differences: invalid %zz in path: oracle 400 html vs rip 404; invalid %zz in query: oracle 500 stacktrace vs rip 200; 20KB URI: oracle 414 vs rip 431; absolute-form, HTTP/1.0, no Host, garbage line, Expect: 100-continue: equivalent. Declared Content-Length of 2 GiB/1 GiB+1/200 MiB with 3 bytes sent: upstream stalls; rip refuses at once with 413 and Connection: close (tikajs-68os.7.7), as it does for any declared length more than 16 MiB over the cap.

Both off by default (no Access-Control-* on any oracle or CLI-rip response). rip with corsOrigin list (verified, second instance): preflight 204 echoes a listed origin, omits it for an unlisted origin, Vary: Origin, Allow-Headers fixed to 'Content-Type, Accept'. Upstream: one origin or '*' via CXF filter; behaviour with cors on not observed.
note: unverified for upstream with cors enabled; CLI has no flag.

divergence: No TLS in rip.

note: Ops feature; plausibly valuable, so not proposed as non-goal.

upstream: Metadata key schema and value shape
divergence: Upstream 4.x: tk:* keys, scalar values unless repeated, tk:content-handler-type, tk:parsed-by, tk:parse-time-millis, tk:embedded-* paths. rip: X-TIKA:* and legacy names, every value an array, responses are 27-45% of the oracle's byte size (r084,r093,r094,r095), with no Content-Length/parsed-by keys. Any client reading tk:content or tk:parsed-by gets nothing.
note: Compatibility mode 3.3.3 (spec/README.md:6) has no switch in the server. tikajs-68os.7.3: the framework keys are Tika 4.x tk:* names and values are a string unless repeated (/rmeta, /meta, /tika JSON, CLI, pipes). Still different: per-format keys (tikajs-68os.10.5), tk:embedded-resource-type/internal-path/embedded-relationship-id are not written, tk:parsed-by holds ripstream parser names, failures are "Name: message" not stack traces. Read from Tika source and the saved oracle responses, not run against a Tika.

upstream: Per-request config headers (X-Tika-OCR*, X-Tika-PDF*, password, writeLimit, maxEmbeddedResources)
divergence: index.ts has no X-Tika-* or password header handling (grep finds none). Oracle also ignored writeLimit and maxEmbeddedResources headers (r073,r106 no change), so no observable delta on the oracle; r076/r077 hit routes rip lacks.
note: unverified whether upstream honours these headers on /tika/text with real OCR/password input.
